9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: medium wide, eye level, MARA (Image 3) sits facing the monitor, tired and still, wearing a green cardigan; DEV (Image 2) is not yet in frame., Observational handheld frame with MARA (Image 3) at the monitor in the foreground; leave open space at the edge for DEV (Image 2) to enter., INT. newsroom (Image 4) - NIGHT, night, newsroom (Image 4), Natural lighting appropriate to night, #8B7355, #CD853F, #DEB887, #F5DEB3, #FFE4B5, Natural documentary style with authentic environments, Natural color with slight desaturation

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
Image 1 (primary): Primary source scene — generate 9 variant shots from this image
